17 An egg of mass 25 g falls vertically downwards from the surface of a table which is 900 mm above
the ground. Air resistance is negligible.
What is the kinetic energy of the egg when it hits the ground?
A
0.023 J
B
0.22 J
C
23 J
D
220 J

hints: Notice the given units: the egg mass is $25 \text{ g}$ and the fall height is $900 \text{ mm}$, so both must be converted to $\text{kg}$ and $\text{m}$ before using an energy equation.
With air resistance negligible, the loss of gravitational potential energy $mgh$ from table surface to ground becomes the gain in kinetic energy of the falling egg.
Set up $E_k = mgh$ with $m = 0.025 \text{ kg}$, $h = 0.90 \text{ m}$ and $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, then check whether your result is near $0.2 \text{ J}$ or near $20$ to $200 \text{ J}$.
walkthrough: Convert the quantities to SI units: $m = 25 \text{ g} = 0.025 \text{ kg}$ and $h = 900 \text{ mm} = 0.90 \text{ m}$.
Use conservation of mechanical energy with no air resistance: kinetic energy at impact equals gravitational potential energy lost, $E_k = mgh$.
Substitute with units: $E_k = 0.025 \times 9.81 \times 0.90$ where the result will be in $\text{J}$.
Calculate the intermediate product: $0.025 \times 0.90 = 0.0225$, then $0.0225 \times 9.81 \approx 0.22 \text{ J}$.
This value matches $0.22 \text{ J}$ to two significant figures. This is option B.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 10. It comes from an extra division by 10 in the $mgh$ calculation or a slip in converting $25 \text{ g}$ and $900 \text{ mm}$.

B.explanation: Equals $mgh$ with $m = 0.025 \text{ kg}$ and $h = 0.90 \text{ m}$, giving about $0.22 \text{ J}$ of kinetic energy at the ground.

C.explanation: About 1000 times too large. It uses mass as $25$ instead of $0.025 \text{ kg}$ while using $h = 0.90 \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: About 1000 times too large. It uses mass as $25$ in grams with $h = 0.90 \text{ m}$, giving $25 \times 9.81 \times 0.90 \approx 220 \text{ J}$.
